letter_note: BC = d.35, BQ = d.47, BD = d.62 - READ OFF THE PAGE, and worth reading off the page rather than sorting. The printed table runs d.35, d.47, d.62 top to bottom and the letters run BC, BQ, BD; alphabetically they are BC, BD, BQ. So the letters are not even in order within one family, and BD - the one that looks like it should follow BC - is the DEEPEST. This is the (family x depth) slot key that printed p.24 established, and it is the first family where getting it wrong by alphabet would have swapped 470 and 620.

data.source_ref: CESAR - 2 Kitchen System.pdf printed p.28 / PDF 30
page_observations: TWO OF THE THREE PLAIN DOOR SUFFIXES NOW AGREE ACROSS THE BASE CLASS. 01 is a plain hinged door at H.48 and at H.78; 25 is a bottom-hung door at H.48 and at H.39. That is two families each, and it is recorded as an observation and derived from nothing - the wall chapter offered exactly this shape of evidence five times before H.120 broke it.

THE MODULARITY DIAGRAM DRAWS THIS FAMILY TWICE SIDE BY SIDE - 78 / 48 + 48 - which is not a stack but a PAIR: the guidelines show two H.48 units filling a 90 or 120 opening, where H.39 is drawn stacked two high. So the low families are not all the same idea, and 'the lower half of a column' is H.39's story and not necessarily this one. Recorded from CESAR - 1 printed p.68; not implemented, and not generalised.
THE PLAIN DOOR STOPS AT W.60 while the bottom-hung door runs to W.120. A hinged door on a 480-tall box gets wide and heavy; the catalog simply does not sell one past 600.
Every row on this page carries the hung glyph, all three depths, all three positions, plus the margin surcharge. No hob glyph anywhere.
